messages.speaker: Maya
messages.text: Morning all. Quick round, then we can dig into the release.

messages.speaker: Tom
messages.text: Yesterday I finished the caching layer for the search endpoint. Response times dropped from 900ms to about 120ms on the staging box.

messages.speaker: Maya
messages.text: That is a big win. Is it measured on the same query set as before?

messages.speaker: Tom
messages.text: Same fifty queries, same warm cache, ran it three times and took the median.

messages.speaker: Ines
messages.text: I spent yesterday chasing the signup bug. Turns out we were sending the confirmation email before the database transaction committed.

messages.speaker: Maya
messages.text: So people clicked the link and the account did not exist yet.

messages.speaker: Ines
messages.text: Exactly. The email now goes out from an after-commit hook, so the row is always there by the time anyone clicks.

messages.speaker: Tom
messages.text: How many users hit that?

messages.speaker: Ines
messages.text: About 40 over two weeks. I have a script to resend to all of them once the fix is live.

messages.speaker: Raf
messages.text: I am still on the migration. Moving the events table to partitioned storage is slower than I hoped.

messages.speaker: Maya
messages.text: What is the blocker?

messages.speaker: Raf
messages.text: The table is 400 million rows and copying it locks writes for too long. I am rewriting it to backfill in batches of fifty thousand.

messages.speaker: Maya
messages.text: Do we need a maintenance window?

messages.speaker: Raf
messages.text: With the batched version, no. It runs in the background and we cut over with a rename at the end.

messages.speaker: Tom
messages.text: Have you tested the rollback path?

messages.speaker: Raf
messages.text: Not yet. That is today. I want to prove we can go back to the old table without losing writes.

messages.speaker: Maya
messages.text: Good. Nothing ships without a tested way back.

messages.speaker: Ines
messages.text: On the release, are we still cutting on Thursday?

messages.speaker: Maya
messages.text: Thursday morning, so we have all day to watch it. Nothing goes out on a Friday.

messages.speaker: Tom
messages.text: The caching change needs a config flag flipped in production. I will document it in the release notes.

messages.speaker: Maya
messages.text: Please make it default off, then we turn it on once we see the dashboards are calm.

messages.speaker: Ines
messages.text: What about the alerting? Last release we found out from a customer.

messages.speaker: Maya
messages.text: That is on me. I am adding a page on error rate above two percent for five minutes straight.

messages.speaker: Raf
messages.text: Can we also alert on the queue depth? The backlog grew for an hour last time before anyone noticed.

messages.speaker: Maya
messages.text: Yes, good call. Queue depth over ten thousand for ten minutes.

messages.speaker: Tom
messages.text: One more thing, the staging database ran out of disk again overnight.

messages.speaker: Raf
messages.text: That is the event table copies I keep leaving behind. I will add a cleanup step to the migration script.

messages.speaker: Maya
messages.text: Fine. Anything anyone is stuck on that we have not covered?

messages.speaker: Ines
messages.text: Nothing from me.

messages.speaker: Tom
messages.text: All good.

messages.speaker: Maya
messages.text: Then we are done. Raf, ping me when the rollback test passes.
